requirements.requirement: Each person sees only what they are entitled to see, decided per request and per field rather than per document.
The platform installs on the client's own server and one deployment serves exactly one company.
Departments are filters inside the one deployment rather than separate systems, so adding another department is configuration with no rebuild or release.
One gate decides who may see what and who may do what for every agent, skill, channel, department, model and connector, and no feature adds a second decision point.
Answers can come from business records in connected systems such as a helpdesk, a CRM and a ledger, reached through typed functions, and not only from documents.
An agent can run multi-step work to completion rather than only answering.
An agent can drive a browser where no API exists for the system it needs.
After an agent acts, the result is verified independently of the agent's own claim of success.
An agent asks a person for approval before a sensitive action and does not perform it until approved.
The client holds their own data and their own model provider keys.
requirements.decision: needs-rupash 80: hosted providers only (Claude, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Moonshot Kimi); no local-only profile

requirements.requirement: Employees ask in the chat tool they already use, not only in a separate application.
The people model has Super Admin, Department Admin, Member, Auditor, Connector Admin and Approver as platform roles, plus an installing partner as a separate kind of principal.
Lark, Slack, Teams, WhatsApp, Telegram, a web widget, email, a REST API and a scheduler all enter through one adapter contract carrying identity binding, a per-channel policy and rich card rendering.

requirements.source: architecture §02 The full architecture; §05 The request lifecycle
requirements.requirement: Every request is identified, entitled, screened, looked up in the cache, routed and given its tool catalogue, in that order, before any model runs.

requirements.source: architecture §02 The full architecture; §05 The request lifecycle
requirements.requirement: A tool the caller cannot use is absent from the catalogue the model sees, computed as the agent's grants intersected with the caller's entitlements, rather than present and refused.
The fast lane answers with no model and no network call, from local data only, in under 1.5 seconds.
The answer lane runs in-process in under 8 seconds with at most one live fetch.

requirements.source: architecture §02 The full architecture; §03 The Python stack
requirements.requirement: The task lane is durable: a task can run for minutes and survives a restart or crash, re-driven by the platform's own driver rather than a commercially licensed server.

requirements.source: architecture §02 The full architecture; owner-confirmed feature list (§19 Automation and autonomy)
requirements.requirement: The orchestrator runs a single loop by default; the model proposes subtasks, an arithmetic fan-out gate decides whether to run them in parallel, and parallel results are merged only after schema validation.
Delegation only ever narrows capabilities, to a depth of at most two and at most eight concurrent children per run.

requirements.source: architecture §02 The full architecture; §04 Core concepts; §05 The request lifecycle
requirements.requirement: Autonomy is a leash rung stored as a database row per agent, target and scope, with three rungs: Shadow simulates and marks the result simulated, Assisted renders the real artefact and suspends for approval, Autonomous proceeds; it is checked before every tool call.
Model routing is deterministic: a tier classifier picks a priority chain of pinned deployments, fallback happens only on a closed set of errors, and a breaker opens on a failure ratio.
Data residency is a hard routing rule: a non-compliant model is skipped and the request is refused if no compliant one remains.
Besides the answer cache, a plan cache stores tool ids only and is filtered through the catalogue projection at execution, and prompts keep a stable prefix so the provider's prompt cache is shared.
A metadata ledger records who, when, capability, scope, rung, tokens and fields removed for every request, holds no content, and is kept for years.
Prompts, tool results and page text go only to a payload store readable under a separate role, masked before they leave the process and kept for 30 days.
A hash-chained audit trail records every grant, leash change and entity merge, and a job proves the chain is unbroken.
An evaluation gate runs a golden question set and permission canaries through the real gate, never against a bare model, and blocks a regression.
The console is organised as Operate (live runs, model matrix, connector health, coverage), Govern (people, scopes, leashes, skills review, audit) and Report (gaps, usage, canaries).
Agents are built in a builder with a form composer, a rehearsal against the real gate, a bounded procedure canvas and a publish gate.
Versioned extension points let a component be plugged in without a core release, and a plug-in can never widen entitlements or see an unredacted result it did not produce.
The gate and the redactor are owned code and are never delegated to a library or a vendor.
Every adopted component has a licence allowing commercial use and modification and is actively maintained, and nothing needs a commercial key in production.
A principal is an authenticated person, service or partner with the platform's own id, mapped from identity-provider and channel identities rather than being the identity provider's id.
A department is a scope: a predicate over rows that can only narrow, never widen, what a grant reaches.
Authorisation is set membership over atomic capabilities: each request computes every (capability, scope) pair the caller holds now, and the hash of that set keys the cache.
Knowledge is human-authored, approved content with an owner, a verified date and a review date, kept distinct from memory, which the system authors.
An uploaded file (PDF, document, image) is parsed and indexed into knowledge, and the platform is its source of truth.

requirements.source: architecture §04 Core concepts; §12 Skills, tools and connectors
requirements.requirement: A skill is a procedure with no side effects of its own: it is loaded by an agent, is not grantable, and anything it does happens through tools the agent's run may use.

requirements.source: architecture §04 Core concepts; §12 Skills, tools and connectors; owner change 2
requirements.requirement: A tool is the only grantable thing; a connector is never granted directly, and attaching a connector to an agent compiles into that agent's ceiling rather than being a second permission system.
A browser or desktop session the agent drives is a surface whose output is untyped, and anything drawn from it carries a weaker, separately labelled guarantee.
Memory is never authoritative over the database: where a memory and a source disagree, the source wins.

requirements.source: architecture §04 Core concepts; §06 Company, departments, users
requirements.requirement: An agent is a named configuration (persona, knowledge, skills, tools, model tier, leash) and a lens over the asker's reach, never an identity with authority of its own.

requirements.source: architecture §04 Core concepts; §11 Agents and templates
requirements.requirement: Every agent is an instance of a signed, versioned, immutable template, and a hand-built agent is an instance of the blank template, so there is one code path.

An automation is a saved task with a schedule, event or webhook trigger that runs as its owner, resolving the owner's live entitlements at every run and suspending when the owner loses a required one.
Every channel event is normalised to one internal shape and deduplicated, so a platform retry never produces a second answer or action.
A channel identity not bound to a principal gets nothing and is told how to bind.
Resolved entitlements are cached for at most 60 seconds and invalidated immediately by any grant write.
What the channel may carry and how strongly the identity was assured are intersected with the caller's entitlements before anything else runs.
An injection classifier scores every input and records the score, and it never permits or blocks a request by itself.
The answer cache key is the question plus the entitlement hash, the agent configuration hash and the policy epoch, so two people with different reach never share a cached answer.
The lane is chosen by deterministic rules and the routing decision is written to the request row, never inferred afterwards.

requirements.source: architecture §05 The request lifecycle; §06 Company, departments, users; owner brief §1 Channels
requirements.requirement: The agent that handles a request is chosen by channel binding, then rules, then a cheap classifier, and a person can also address an agent they are allowed to use directly.
An Assisted action shows the approver the real artefact that will be produced, not the tool call.

requirements.source: architecture §05 The request lifecycle; §02 The full architecture
requirements.requirement: Redaction walks every typed result depth-first, deletes each field outside the caller's mask at any nesting depth, and drops anything without an entity tag, failing closed.
Only the post-redaction payload is ever sent to a trace.
Every answer carries citations with their freshness and a trace reference that explains it.

requirements.source: architecture §06 Company, departments, users; owner-confirmed feature list (§19 Administration)
requirements.requirement: The organisation is modelled as one company, its departments, teams within departments, and the users in each.

requirements.source: architecture §06 Company, departments, users; §07 Roles and permissions
requirements.requirement: A company-wide agent is published and retired only by a Super Admin and can be found and used by everyone in the company.

requirements.source: architecture §06 Company, departments, users; §07 Roles and permissions
requirements.requirement: A department agent is created and published by that department's Department Admin and can be found and used only by members of that department.
Any member can build a personal agent, which only its creator can see or use until it is published.

requirements.source: architecture §06 Company, departments, users; §10 Knowledge and RAG
requirements.requirement: Audience is not authority: visibility decides who can find and invoke an agent, and what a run returns is always the calling person's entitlement, never the agent's or its creator's, so a company-wide agent that reaches finance data answers a junior member with only what that junior may see.

requirements.source: architecture §06 Company, departments, users; owner change 1
requirements.requirement: A run's reach is the caller's entitlements intersected with the agent's ceiling; the ceiling can only shrink the caller's set, and the agent is not an input to the entitlement resolver, the entitlement hash or the redactor.

Roles govern platform verbs (publish, install, appoint, read audit metadata) and are a compiled constant rather than editable rows, while access to data is governed only by (capability, scope) grants.

requirements.source: architecture §07 Roles and permissions; needs-rupash 16; needs-rupash 39
requirements.requirement: No role implies any data capability, including Super Admin: holding a role grants no reach, navigation is computed from grants, and a directory or staff list never sets a role.
A Super Admin holds a company-scoped role to publish company-wide agents, change the capability catalogue, confirm role nominations and disable principals.
The platform always keeps at least two Super Admins and refuses to revoke the last ones.
A Department Admin role cannot be granted without naming the department scope it runs.
A Department Admin approves publications within their own department, and a publication to the whole company is approved by a Super Admin.
A Department Admin can grant capabilities only within their own department's scope, never wider.

requirements.source: architecture §07 Roles and permissions; §06 Company, departments, users
requirements.requirement: A Department Admin adopts the agents left without an owner when someone in their department leaves.
A Department Admin can lower a leash at once but cannot raise one beyond the agent's ceiling; raising needs evidence and a named approver.
A Member asks questions, builds personal agents and owns the delegations they create.
An Auditor reads the whole metadata plane, including every Super Admin action, and never any content.
A Connector Admin installs connectors and binds and rotates credential references, gains no agent or knowledge access from the role, and is deliberately a different person from the Super Admins.

requirements.source: architecture §07 Roles and permissions; needs-rupash 14; needs-rupash 16
requirements.requirement: An Approver (a department-scoped role) approves Assisted actions only within their own entitlement, the approve permission rather than the role decides, and the prepared action they see is rendered at the approver's own reach.
A contractor or external person is a principal attribute with a mandatory expiry date, not a separate role.

requirements.source: architecture §07 Roles and permissions; needs-rupash 15; needs-rupash 23
requirements.requirement: An installing partner is a principal with zero standing entitlement that works only through time-boxed break-glass sessions, each with a stated reason, recorded on its own immutable audit chain and notified to the client.

requirements.source: architecture §07 Roles and permissions; owner-confirmed feature list (§19 Administration: six platform roles plus stewardship)
requirements.requirement: Knowledge ownership is a per-object stewardship relation rather than a global Curator role, and the steward is the person notified about access to that object.
Building an agent is unrestricted; governance applies at publication, which is where approval is required.
A service account or API key is a standing delegation that acts at its owner's live entitlements and never holds grants of its own.
A deputy is a time-boxed role grant of at most 30 days that cannot itself appoint a further deputy.
Visibility has three planes: existence and configuration are governed by role, content only by entitlement, so a Super Admin sees no document body or field value without a grant.
Credential values are visible to nobody, ever: a credential is written once and never read back.
A Super Admin may grant themselves a capability, and doing so writes a loud audit event and notifies the object's steward.

requirements.source: architecture §07 Roles and permissions (the mover case)
requirements.requirement: When someone changes department, their entitlements re-resolve on their next request with no manual step.

requirements.source: architecture §07 Roles and permissions (the mover case)
requirements.requirement: A person's personal agents follow them when they change department.

requirements.source: architecture §07 Roles and permissions (the mover case)
requirements.requirement: When someone changes department, each delegation they own is re-evaluated, and one that would now exceed their entitlements is suspended rather than silently narrowed.

requirements.source: architecture §07 Roles and permissions (the mover case)
requirements.requirement: Cached answers keyed on a mover's old entitlement hash become unreachable by construction, with no purge.

requirements.source: architecture §07 Roles and permissions (the mover case); §13 Memory
requirements.requirement: A memory formed under a capability set is re-checked at read time, so once someone's entitlements change, memories formed under the old set stop being replayed to them without any purge job.

requirements.source: architecture §10 Knowledge and RAG; §08 Data: what we store
requirements.requirement: When someone changes department, the department knowledge they could read stops resolving on their next request with no reindex or cache purge, because the scope predicate is evaluated live.

requirements.source: architecture §08 Data: what we store; _requirements-audit section 3
requirements.requirement: Connector data is not synced: the platform stores only its own local tier (identity, capabilities, audit, leash state, agent configuration, uploaded knowledge, memory, entity registry) and a bounded projection, and fetches everything else live.
The projection holds at most 12 fields per entity type, limited to record ids, join keys, status values, timestamps, display labels of at most 120 characters and the source's visibility predicate.
Email addresses, phone numbers, postal addresses, identity numbers, bank details and salary are on a permanent deny list and are never projected, with no exception.
Ticket bodies, conversations, invoice lines, contracts, CRM notes, attachments and custom fields are read live for the request and never stored by the platform.

The platform stores each source's visibility predicate rather than a resolved access list and evaluates it against the live entitlement set, so a department change returns a different row set with zero writes.
A field is projected only when the fast lane must filter, sort or count on it and the source signals when it changes; a source with no change signal gets no projected fields.
Calls to each source stay within that source's documented rate ceilings, which are shared with the client's other integrations.

Questions that span many records, such as which clients have a high-priority ticket open longer than five days, are answerable from locally projected headers even where the source's search caps its results.
The same organisation recorded under different names in different systems resolves to one canonical entity, and one client may legitimately keep several names.
People and projects are resolved across systems by the same cascade as organisations.

Matching runs strongest evidence first: a hard identifier (business registration number, tax id, web domain, verified phone) links automatically, a normalised name links only with a second corroborating field, a fuzzy match links only above the upper threshold with corroboration, and the band between thresholds goes to a person.
A reviewer deciding an ambiguous match sees the evidence as a weighted plain-language list, such as same web domain strong, similar name weak, different phone negative.

Free-mail domains are blocklisted as evidence, non-English names are compared by edit distance and a multilingual phonetic method rather than an English-only one, and a normalised name under four characters always goes to review.
Every merge is reversible: the complete prior state of the affected links and aliases is written to an append-only record first, a merge only moves pointers, and unmerge restores from that record.
A canonical id, once issued, resolves forever through a forwarding pointer, so an old citation or memory never dangles.
Known junk values can never cause a link, each identifier type has a cap on distinct values per entity, and which identifier wins in a collision is configured.
A merge that would join entities carrying financial records never links automatically, whatever its score, and needs a person.
When records cannot be confirmed as the same entity, the agent says so, names both records, does not combine their figures, and offers the review link.
The resolver holds hashed join keys, never full contact records.
Match weights are calibrated offline on a weekly schedule, and online scoring runs in plain SQL in about a millisecond with no machine-learning dependency in the request path.

Business records are reached through typed tools whose column list is compiled from the caller's capabilities before the query runs, so a hidden field is never in the SQL and never leaves the database.
No model ever writes SQL against a business database.
Documents are searched by full-text and vector search together, fused by rank.
The scope filter is applied inside the retrieval query, so out-of-scope knowledge is absent from results rather than ranked lower, with row-level security as a second wall.
Parsing is layout-aware, so tables inside PDF contracts survive into the chunks that are searched.
A person with a narrow scope still gets relevant results rather than a near-empty set caused by filtering after the vector index scan.
A citation for a business record names the record, the field and the time it was read.
Every knowledge item carries verified-by, verified-at and review-by, shown as a badge on the answer, and a scheduled job opens re-verification tasks when the review date arrives.
All uploaded knowledge lands in one knowledge layer with no separate store per department; a scope predicate on each item decides who reaches it.
Company-level knowledge is set by a Super Admin, or proposed by a Department Admin and approved by a Super Admin, and everyone reaches it subject to field-level redaction.
Department knowledge is set by that department's Department Admin and reachable only within that department's scope.
Personal knowledge is reachable only by the person who uploaded it until it is published.
Uploading is not publishing: knowledge a department adds stays within that department's scope by default, and widening it is a deliberate act that records an owner and a review date.

A company-wide agent has no standing access to knowledge: someone asking it about another department's material gets nothing or only the parts they may see, with the rest shown as locked and never counted.

requirements.source: architecture §10 Knowledge and RAG; owner change 3
requirements.requirement: Pricing is classified at column level, so the whole company sees sell prices while cost and margin columns are restricted, from one price list rather than several near-identical copies.
An installed agent is a pinned template reference plus an overlay, and each field records who last set it.

A template manifest declares the capabilities it needs but never grants them, and capabilities, leash ceiling, egress, connector authentication and the surface flag are sealed against a template by a database constraint.
Installing a template runs its golden question set through the real gate twice, once as the installing administrator and once as a deliberately low-privilege user.
Missing connectors do not block an install: the agent is pinned to Shadow with an amber badge listing what is missing.
An agent whose declared tools all fail to resolve raises a hard error instead of answering from the model's general knowledge.

requirements.source: architecture §11 Agents and templates; owner brief §5 Agents
requirements.requirement: The template catalogue ships role templates (business analyst, pre-sales, project manager, UI and UX designer, HTML, WordPress, Laravel and Shopify developer, content uploader, tester) and operational templates (internal helpdesk, site health sentinel, support ticket agent, project status reporter, capacity and hours analyst, quote and proposal drafter, receivables and renewal chaser, accountant, SEO, SEM, SMM, knowledge gap curator).

requirements.source: architecture §11 Agents and templates; owner change 9
requirements.requirement: The first agent delivered is one complete Maintenance agent on the owner's install, with a chat channel, the ticket desk, uploaded maintenance knowledge, one workflow and one approval.

The receivables and renewal chaser and the accountant agent stay pinned to Shadow at manifest level because they touch money, and the SEM agent is Shadow-pinned with a person committing every ad budget change.
The SEO and SMM agents read and draft by default, and publishing is a separate grant.
What an agent learns is written to a reviewable queue as typed, evidenced, machine-authored changes, kept permanently separable from what the client configured.
A department lead approves or rejects the gated learning proposed for their department's agents.

A connector can use any of four transports (an MCP server, a REST or OpenAPI spec with a field mapping, a read-only database credential against allowlisted views, or a sandboxed custom adapter), and all four return the same entity-tagged typed contract.
A connection is scoped when it is made, for example to one folder rather than a whole drive.

requirements.source: architecture §12 Skills, tools and connectors; §02 The full architecture
requirements.requirement: Connectors are read-only by default, and writing to a source is a separate deliberate grant shown when the connector is connected.
Every tool declares whose identity it runs as, and it runs as the requesting person by default.
A third-party tool server is pinned by a hash of its full manifest including tool descriptions, so a silent redefinition fails closed on reconnect.

requirements.source: architecture §12 Skills, tools and connectors; §04 Core concepts; owner D4
requirements.requirement: A skill imported from a repository, a URL or an upload is not executable until a named reviewer approves it, and an administrator approving a skill they imported themselves is allowed and recorded as such.
An agent sees only skill names and descriptions until it needs one, and loads the full instructions on demand.
A skill's scripts run only through one execution tool that carries the sandbox, the leash and output redaction like any other tool call.
Session memory holds the current conversation and working state, is visible only to the asker, and dies with the thread.
Persistent memory holds facts about people and entities, preferences and recurring context, is visible by scope, and lasts until changed.
Adaptive memory holds procedural learning from outcomes within the agent's scope, loses confidence on a schedule unless reinforced, and a reinforced memory regains its confidence.
Nothing is promoted from a narrower to a wider scope, personal to department or department to company, without a person approving it.

requirements.source: architecture §13 Memory; owner brief §8 Memory and Context; owner change 5
requirements.requirement: The context for one turn is assembled in one place from the conversation, the task, the project, what is remembered about the asker, the agent's memory and company knowledge, each read at the asker's current reach, with project and user context re-read every time.
Each agent is configured with which kinds of memory and context it may read and write, and a run cannot read a kind its configuration leaves out.

Learning never fine-tunes a model or lets an agent write to itself; which oversight a learned change needs is decided automatically by its blast radius, and no setting can move a kind of change to a lower oversight tier.
Learning that only narrows, personalises or re-ranks for one person applies automatically: user preferences, retrieval boosts and demotions, and entity links corroborated by a hard identifier.

requirements.source: architecture §13 Memory; owner brief §11 Learning; owner-confirmed feature list (§19 Agents: agents that learn, via a reviewable queue)
requirements.requirement: Fast-path rules and procedural shortcuts that use only tools the agent already holds are first computed in shadow beside the real answer and not used.
Widening scope, changing company knowledge, raising a leash, a merge that crosses a money boundary, and anything that adds a capability or tool always wait for a person.
Automatic and self-promoted learning is reported in a weekly digest saying what each agent learned and why, with one-click undo on every item.
The gated learning review queue has a budget, and the console charts its size and raises an alarm when it keeps growing.

Implicit signals are captured from the first migration: a question re-asked in different words within minutes, an answer copied, a contradicting follow-up, an escalation to a person, a person taking over an Assisted action, a ticket reopened within a set number of days, and an approval rejected with a reason.

requirements.source: architecture §13 Memory; owner brief §11 Learning; owner change 8
requirements.requirement: A person can mark an answer helpful or unhelpful in one action on the console and every channel, and the mark is counted but changes nothing by itself.
A learned fact that two records are the same organisation lands in the entity registry, not in memory.
A learned procedure becomes a proposed change to a skill, reviewed and versioned like code, never a hidden weight.
A learned preference belongs to one person and is never shared with or applied to anyone else.

requirements.source: architecture §13 Memory; §08 Data: what we store; owner brief §8 Memory and Context
requirements.requirement: The system never learns or remembers a field value from a connected source; it learns patterns and pointers only.
A newer observation that contradicts an older memory supersedes it, and the older one is marked superseded rather than removed, so what the agent used to believe and when it changed stays visible.
When a memory disagrees with the source system, the source wins at once and the memory is demoted and flagged for review that day, with no decay period.

requirements.source: architecture §13 Memory; owner-confirmed feature list (§19 Memory: inspect, edit and delete any memory)
requirements.requirement: Every agent has a Memory tab listing what it has learned with the evidence, confidence and date, where a person can edit or delete any item, and anything deleted is gone from retrieval immediately.
A department admin sees and controls the same memory and learning view for their own department's agents.
Nothing is learned that a person cannot read back in plain language.

A person correcting an answer may give the right answer, which is held as a permission-protected learning candidate and changes no knowledge, rule or memory until the owner of the affected knowledge approves it.

A department admin gets every console screen the requirements call for, narrowed to their own department, including a stop control for their own department, while screens whose subject is the whole installation are not offered to them.

requirements.source: architecture §05 The request lifecycle; owner brief §1 Channels; owner change 1
requirements.requirement: An agent answers only on the channels an administrator enabled for it, and a message reaching it on any other channel is refused before it runs.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Asking and answering / Natural-language questions over company data
requirements.requirement: A person can ask a question in natural language and get an answer drawn from the company's data.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Asking and answering / Answers from live business records, not just documents
requirements.requirement: An answer can be drawn from live records in the company's business systems, not only from documents.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Asking and answering / Field-level redaction per person
requirements.requirement: Each person sees only the fields of a record they are entitled to, with the rest removed before the answer is composed.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Asking and answering / Citations to record and field, with freshness
requirements.requirement: Every answer cites the record and field or document passage it came from, with when it was read and whether it is stale.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Asking and answering / Four distinct "I don't know" states
requirements.requirement: An answer that cannot be given says which of four states applies: nothing retrieved, retrieved but not answerable, nothing connected, or not entitled.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Asking and answering / Fast lane: instant answers with no model call
requirements.requirement: Common question shapes are answered instantly by rules held as data, with no model call and no tool catalogue.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Asking and answering / Streaming with named progress steps
requirements.requirement: Answers stream to the person with named progress steps in their own language, citations before prose, and reasoning never streamed.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Asking and answering / Conversation history and search
requirements.requirement: A person can see and search their own conversation history, continued across channels.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Asking and answering / Escalation to a human with full context
requirements.requirement: A question can be escalated to a person who receives who asked, what, what was tried and what is needed, in their own channel, with a timeout.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Asking and answering / Request-access route when refused
requirements.requirement: A person refused access is offered a route to request it, where the owner sees the question and the asker learns nothing more.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Agents / Global, department and personal agents
requirements.requirement: Agents exist at company, department and personal level, and a personal agent is visible to nobody else unless shared.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Agents / Pre-built template catalogue, install in minutes
requirements.requirement: A catalogue of ready-made agent templates can be installed and answering within minutes.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Agents / Role templates for every agency discipline
requirements.requirement: There is an agent template for every service discipline the company delivers, including maintenance, SEO, sales, finance, support and project management.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Agents / Custom agents via the form composer
requirements.requirement: A department admin or member builds a custom agent without code through a form composer.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Agents / Procedure canvas for authored steps
requirements.requirement: Authored step-by-step procedures can be drawn on a bounded canvas that produces a skill, with scope predicates as the only condition and no code node.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Agents / Assign skills, tools, connectors, knowledge
requirements.requirement: Skills, tools, connectors and knowledge are each assigned to an agent separately, and a run uses only what is assigned.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Agents / Per-agent model tier and instructions
requirements.requirement: Each agent carries its own model tier and instructions, and its run uses them.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Agents / Save any agent as a private template
requirements.requirement: Any agent can be saved as a private template after a leak scan of its literals, never carrying memory.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Agents / Template versioning with opt-in upgrade
requirements.requirement: Templates are versioned, and an installed agent upgrades only when its owner opts in, resolving conflicts path by path.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Agents / Agents that learn, via a reviewable queue
requirements.requirement: Agents improve from what they learn, and what they learn passes through a queue a person reviews.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Agents / Rehearsal against real gate with mocked tools
requirements.requirement: A draft agent can be rehearsed against the real gate, leash and redactor with tools replayed from recordings, so nothing real happens.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Agents / Publish gate with permission canaries
requirements.requirement: Publishing an agent is blocked unless system-authored permission canaries pass, with author tests advisory.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Skills and tools / SKILL.md folder format
requirements.requirement: A skill is a folder in the SKILL.md format with validated frontmatter.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Skills and tools / Import from GitHub, URL or upload
requirements.requirement: A skill can be imported from a repository at a pinned commit, from a URL, or from an uploaded archive.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Skills and tools / Review queue before anything executes
requirements.requirement: An imported or edited skill cannot execute until it has passed a review queue with a diff.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Skills and tools / Skill versioning and diffs

requirements.requirement: There are six fixed platform roles plus a data steward who is granted each connected source's capabilities.

requirements.requirement: People sign in through the company's identity provider by SAML or OIDC.

requirements.requirement: Joining, moving department and leaving each update what a person can reach, their agents, automations, memory and sessions.

requirements.requirement: A person can deputise for another for at most a set time, one level deep, and the delegation lapses by itself.

requirements.requirement: Administrators see all activity, filterable by department and by user, with a department admin seeing their own department's activity.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Administration / Hash-chained audit log
requirements.requirement: Every grant, denial, leash change, merge, publish and emergency access is written to a hash-chained audit log that is verified to be unbroken.

requirements.requirement: Data is kept per retention policy, can be exported and deleted on request, and a legal hold suspends deletion.
