requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Administration / Redaction-rate and canary reporting
requirements.requirement: The console reports how often fields were redacted and the results of permission canary runs.

requirements.source: owner feature list, architecture §19 Feature list: Administration / Install, upgrade, backup and restore tooling
requirements.requirement: There is tooling to install, upgrade, back up and restore an install.
A large task can be split into subtasks that run across several agents in parallel and are merged into one answer.
Whether a task runs in parallel is decided by deterministic arithmetic over a dependency graph weighted by estimated cost and by the shared context a split would duplicate, never by the model.
When any fan-out condition fails the run collapses to a single agent loop, and the single loop is the default rather than the exception.
The fan-out gate's inputs and verdict are recorded on the run so the parallel-versus-serial choice can be audited against its cost.
Every subtask carries a contract of objective, output schema, tool hints and scope predicate.
A subtask result that does not validate against its schema is a failed step and never a merge input, and free prose is not a permitted subtask output.
A delegated child's permissions are computed in the database as parent intersected with agent intersected with subtask, and the database rejects any delegation row that is not a subset of its parent.
The orchestrator has no operation that can grant a permission.
Delegation depth is capped at two and concurrency at eight subtasks per run.

requirements.source: architecture §14 Multi-agent execution; architecture §25 Capacity, failure and SLOs (Admission control)
requirements.requirement: A global parallelism budget bounds concurrent subtasks across all runs and is enforced centrally before work starts, so many users each fanning out cannot exhaust the host.

A cross-department request from someone holding both scopes runs as one plan with both filters; someone holding only one scope gets what they are entitled to, a stated reason for the gap and a request-access route.
Agents can navigate, log in, read the screen, fill forms, take multi-step decisions, verify the result and report back on client systems that expose no usable API.
A browser write is treated as an attempt and is reported as done only after it has been verified out of band against the target system.

Read-only browsing (checking a client portal, reading a dashboard no API exposes, pulling a status page) ships before browser writes, and writes stay behind the envelope, enforcer and out-of-band verifier.
The browser control plane that holds the plan, the capability set and the target registry never reads page content.
The browser runner that reads pages runs in an ephemeral sandboxed container with its own network namespace, is destroyed at run end, and holds no authority.

A deterministic guard containing no model sits between planner and runner, with policy compiled at container start and immutable afterwards, validating each action against the snapshot just produced and the envelope's write verbs and counts.
All browser egress passes through a proxy the container cannot route around and is denied by default except to the approved envelope's origins.
Every browser session is fully recorded under a retention policy and its actions are written to the hash-chained audit.
A person approves a browser envelope once, shown as a readable diff of the plan and its declared writes on an approval card, rather than approving step by step.
A browser run that breaches its approved envelope is interrupted and asks again, and a run inside its envelope is never re-interrupted.
The browser agent reads the accessibility tree rather than screenshots, so a credential shown on a page cannot reach the model through an image.
Browser credentials, including one-time codes, resolve by reference at the execution boundary, substitute only on their own origin, and never enter a prompt, message history or log.
Browser success is never the agent's own claim: a verifier builds its rubric from the goal before seeing the trajectory and is tuned against false positives.
A browser skill is refused for any domain that has a registered API tool unless the skill carries an exception with a named approver and an expiry.
An agent is never attached to a staff member's own logged-in browser profile.

requirements.source: architecture §15 Browser and computer use; owner brief change 6 and the owner brief §9 example (check whether a client website is working)
requirements.requirement: A website check uses plain HTTP first (status, redirects, certificate, response time) and a read-only browser only where a rendered page must be inspected, with computer use as a last resort.

requirements.source: architecture §15 Browser and computer use (heading and feature group title); owner brief §9
requirements.requirement: An agent can operate an allowlisted desktop application inside an isolated virtual desktop, with every action recorded, every write held for approval and no route to any other application or network.
One brain serves Lark, Slack, Teams, WhatsApp, Telegram, a web widget, email and the API, and every channel enters the same agent runtime.
A channel gateway only terminates its platform's wire protocol and applies no entitlement, redaction or policy of its own.
A chat identity is bound to a person only by presenting a single-use, expiring nonce minted inside an authenticated web session, and a code is never sent to a number that asked for one.

In a group chat the shared message is computed at the floor of everyone present and each viewer receives their own body through the platform's private mechanism, falling back to a link into the web app where the gate re-runs under that viewer.
An asynchronous task result re-runs the entitlement computation at send time rather than trusting the moment it was authorised.
Per-channel policy decides which sensitivity classes a channel may carry at all.

requirements.source: architecture §18 Builder and console (Three surfaces table: channels are for asking, answering and approving in Lark and WhatsApp); owner brief change 7
requirements.requirement: Approvals are decided only in the console, the member application or on a Lark card, never by WhatsApp or email.

The model tier is classified deterministically from tool count, estimated context, lane, an explicit user request and whether the scope touches residency-restricted data, never by a model call, so retrieved text cannot influence routing.
Each tier has an ordered chain (default, next model at the same provider, next model, next provider) held as data and editable in the console.

Fallback to the next rung fires only on a closed set of failures (connection error, timeout, rate limit, server error, context exceeded), never because an answer looked weak, and a model's content refusal is answered once through abstention rather than retried on another model.
Every model attempt appends a row, so the executed fallback chain can be reconstructed from one join.
The provider circuit breaker opens on a failure ratio over a window rather than failures per minute, a background prober keeps an idle but broken provider visible, and cooldown backs off with jitter.
Alerts fire on fallback depth rather than only on final failure.
A scope carrying a residency constraint never routes outside it: non-compliant rungs are skipped rather than degraded to, and the request is refused when no compliant rung remains.
Agent control flow is decided by the model at run time over a catalogue projected per request, so an agent is authored as a form and never as a drawn graph of edges the runtime would have to honour.
Everything an author picks in the composer is re-derived on the server, so an authored list is intent and never authorisation.
A completed run can be opened as a read-only trace graph of what actually happened.
Publishing an agent that widens its grants demotes it to Shadow and needs a second approver, while editing only its instructions publishes without demotion.
The install wizard and every template configuration screen are generated from the manifest schema, so adding a template field needs no hand-built screen.

Deterministic automations (a trigger then fixed steps, with no model deciding control flow) can be drawn on an optional canvas that runs sandboxed with allowlisted egress and no database credentials, calls tools through the API so the gate runs on every call, and is enabled per install by configuration rather than a fork.
No builder surface lets an administrator run code that bypasses the gate: a flow cannot reach data outside the caller's entitlements and the procedure canvas has no code node.
The Operate screens show live runs, the model matrix and provider health, connector health, knowledge coverage and staleness, and the queue and automations.
The Govern screens show people and grants, scopes and departments, agents with leash state and promotion history, skills and templates with the review queue, and the audit.
The Report screens show questions and gaps, usage and cost, and quality and canaries.
Console reads are tool calls that require capabilities, and console rows are entity-tagged so redaction applies to reports exactly as to answers.
A report's audience is intersected with the caller's scope and never unioned, including the options offered in its filters.

A Super Admin can narrow every console view by department and by user, and a Department Admin sees the same screens with the scope pinned and cross-department rows absent, as a query predicate rather than a second frontend.

Observability keeps a content-free metadata ledger with long retention and a separate payload store kept thirty days behind its own role, with an audit row written before every payload read, so the console holds no payloads of its own.
Every request declares its traffic class at ingress with no default, so a new channel cannot be added without stating what kind of traffic it produces.

There are three authored surfaces (the admin console, the agent workspace and the member application) plus the chat channels, differing by who signs in, with entitlement deciding reach identically in all four.
The agent workspace has seven tabs (Conversations, Automations, People, Knowledge, Memory, Artifacts, Settings) and the member application nine screens.
Knowledge and learning screens exist for both admin roles: a Department Admin sees their own department's rows and the Super Admin sees every row in the company.
A Super Admin sees the complete inventory by role: every agent, skill, knowledge item, connector, grant and learning, with its owner, scope, freshness and audience.

Opening the content of another department's item is a capability separate from seeing it in the inventory, granted by default on a single-company install, revocable, and written to the audit ledger on every use.

An agent composes persona, knowledge, connectors, skills, channels, model policy, ceiling, leash, memory, automations and artifacts, each stored as a reference with a pinned version, so a fix reaches every instance when a version is promoted and a repository push alone changes nothing live.

Each agent attachment has a named editor: the owner for persona, knowledge (within their own scope), skills (after review), memory and automations; the department admin for connectors, channels, ceiling and leash; the super admin for model policy.
An agent's knowledge is a scope predicate, never a list of documents, previewed by how many items it currently matches.
A connector an agent needs that its department has not granted is shown as requested, not attached, and attaching checks the capability at attach time.
An agent can attach only pinned skill versions from the approved library, and an unapproved skill is offered with a route to the review queue instead.
An agent's channels are references intersected with its ceiling before they are offered, and a message from a channel not enabled for the agent is refused before it runs.
An agent's leash is a rung per target and scope set by the department admin, and a money boundary cannot rise without two approvers.
An agent's memory is readable text with a diff per revision, changed by the agent owner, and a person may delete memory about themselves.
Automations are owned by an agent and run on a named principal, never on the agent itself.

Availability (who can find and invoke an agent) and ceiling (the widest reach any run may have) are separate blocks that never merge, and adding people to availability gives them no data they could not already reach because a run resolves to the caller's reach intersected with the ceiling.
A preview-as-a-person control shows what a chosen person's run of the agent would return, computed by the real gate and never by a separate estimator.

An artifact (report, deck, export, image) inherits the entitlement of the run that produced it, with field-level redaction applied when it is produced so it never holds more than its caller could see.
Re-downloading an artifact re-checks the requester's current entitlement rather than trusting the original link.
An artifact's retention follows the classification of the most sensitive input that fed it.
Artifacts are superseded and archived, never edited, so their provenance stays intact.
The permission gate, catalogue projection and redaction are the product's own code and are never delegated to a third-party component or a connector.
The durable execution engine sits behind the product's own adapter, so replacing it changes one file.
Retrieval runs in the one database with no second datastore, and the scope filter is inside the query rather than applied afterwards.
Document embeddings are computed locally, off the request path, so document content is not sent to a third party to be embedded.
Online entity matching runs in plain SQL in about a millisecond with no machine-learning dependency in the request path, calibrated offline weekly.
Memory access is controlled by the capability set recorded on each memory, never by partitioning memory by an id.
The model gateway library is used only as a driver: routing authority, budgets and residency stay in the product, and no model proxy service sits in the path.
PII detection is a signal used to scrub free text before third-party egress and is never an authorisation boundary.
Browser sandboxing works on hosts without kernel virtualisation, with stronger kernel-level isolation used only where the host provides it.
Secrets are issued as leases scoped to the agent, action, scope and run, and revoked when the run ends.
Trace payloads are masked inside the application before any span leaves the process, never relying on the tracing server to mask them.
Evaluations run through the product's own gate, so a passing evaluation proves something about redaction and not just about a prompt.
No dependency that is archived, stale or under a licence that forbids commercial use and modification is adopted, checked in CI.

Each install profile (small, medium, large by staff count) has a recorded machine size, database memory settings, pool sizes, worker concurrency, browser memory cap, yearly disk growth and backup target.
The application and the job worker use separate database pools, the worker's in session mode so its notifications keep working.
Model provider client timeouts and retries are overridden per lane (about 25 seconds and one retry on the answer lane) rather than left at library defaults.
Bulk document parsing runs in a memory-bounded worker and is throttled, so ingestion cannot exhaust memory or slow chat.

The same code deploys as a lite profile (database, app, worker, proxy, identity, ledger only) or a full profile (adding tracing, payload store, object storage, browser runner and automation) by choosing a compose file.

requirements.source: architecture §22 Making it faster and more flexible; architecture §27 Open questions (not measured)
requirements.requirement: From the first stage every answer records time to first token, per-stage timings, the reasoning-versus-output token split, rate-limit responses and its lane, so the lane split and output tokens per answer are measured rather than assumed.

requirements.source: architecture §22 Making it faster and more flexible
requirements.requirement: The tool prefix sent to the model is a byte-identical union of every tool followed by only the entitled subset, so the provider cache is shared across all users while the cached bytes carry no per-user data.

requirements.source: architecture §22 Making it faster and more flexible
requirements.requirement: New fast-lane rules are data rows that a department admin can add without a release, and the fast lane's share is measured excluding machine traffic.

requirements.source: architecture §22 Making it faster and more flexible
requirements.requirement: The serial guard checkpoints are collapsed into a single pass where semantics allow, without losing detection coverage.

requirements.source: architecture §22 Making it faster and more flexible
requirements.requirement: A plan cache stores tool ids only and is a hint filtered through catalogue projection at execution, never an authorisation.

requirements.source: architecture §22 Making it faster and more flexible
requirements.requirement: Named progress steps never reveal a source the viewer may not know exists.

requirements.source: architecture §22 Making it faster and more flexible
requirements.requirement: An answer cache is used only once source epochs and a policy epoch are in its key, so tightening a field policy immediately stops a cached answer disclosing the revoked field.

requirements.source: architecture §22 Making it faster and more flexible
requirements.requirement: Semantic answer caching and any cache keyed without the entitlement hash are forbidden by construction.

requirements.source: architecture §22 Making it faster and more flexible
requirements.requirement: Scaling work (console read replica, ledger partitioning, materialised report views, local model hosting) is built only when its written trigger is met.

requirements.source: architecture §22 Making it faster and more flexible
requirements.requirement: A new connector or channel ships without a core release through versioned extension points.

requirements.source: architecture §22 Making it faster and more flexible
requirements.requirement: Every external vendor sits behind the product's own adapter so swapping it costs one file, and anything an operator tunes is configuration data in the database rather than code, so tuning is not a deploy.
An install runs as Docker Compose on any Linux server or the client's own hardware, not tied to one cloud provider.
Server requirements state the region (close to the company and its source systems), NVMe storage and the memory the deployment panel itself takes.
An install needs no CDN in front to have TLS, can run with no inbound ports through a tunnel, and a public web widget can be fronted by DDoS and WAF protection.

requirements.source: architecture §23 Hosting, delivery and recovery; owner brief change 9 and D3
requirements.requirement: Runtime secrets (connector credentials and browser session material) live in the vault with per-run leases and an audit trail, never in environment variables, and the vault and the worker run on the owner's install.
CI runs lint, type checks, tests, a migration check and the permission canaries, then builds, signs and publishes the container image.
The server pulls its update and the code host never pushes to it, so no inbound access to a client's server and no production credential is held by the code host.
Each install pins a release tag, so one client can stay on an older release while an urgent fix ships to another.
Per-install configuration is one variables file kept in a separate private repository, never in the application repository.
Secrets are minted per install, never copied between clients and never stored in git.
Migrations run before the new image takes traffic and stay backward-compatible for one release, so rolling back is re-pinning the previous tag and takes about a minute.
An update drains in-flight work before the old version stops and passes a readiness gate before it takes traffic.
Every install is checked, not remembered, for the four things a copied deployment silently carries: platform project files, temporary CLI state, git remotes and scheduled jobs.
The database is backed up by continuous write-ahead-log archiving with daily incremental and weekly full backups, and the object store and configuration daily with deduplication.
Backups always go off the host and are encrypted at rest with a key the client holds.

requirements.source: architecture §23 Hosting, delivery and recovery; needs-rupash 60
requirements.requirement: Backup retention fits inside the promise made to a person whose data is erased: thirty daily copies and weekly copies up to thirty-five days.
Every week the latest backup is restored into a scratch container, migrated, checked with a smoke query and a permission canary, timed as the measured recovery time, and destroyed.
The console recovery panel shows the last backup, the last verified restore and the measured recovery time against the profile target, and offers a one-click drill.
An alert fires when backup age exceeds the profile's recovery point, and a louder alert fires when a restore verification fails.

requirements.source: architecture §24 Quotas, budgets and cost control
requirements.requirement: The company has a monthly token and currency ceiling set by the Super Admin, with a hard stop and alerts at 70 and 90 per cent.

requirements.source: architecture §24 Quotas, budgets and cost control
requirements.requirement: Each department's budget is a share of the company budget, and departments cannot borrow from each other without an explicit transfer.

requirements.source: architecture §24 Quotas, budgets and cost control
requirements.requirement: Each user has a daily and monthly allowance set by their Department Admin, with a fair-share cap so one person cannot drain the department.

requirements.source: architecture §24 Quotas, budgets and cost control
requirements.requirement: Each agent has a per-run and a per-day cost ceiling set by whoever publishes it.

requirements.source: architecture §24 Quotas, budgets and cost control
requirements.requirement: Every budget level is a versioned, audited row editable in the console, never a constant in code.

requirements.source: architecture §24 Quotas, budgets and cost control
requirements.requirement: Before work starts the router estimates a request's cost from lane, tier, expected tool count and retrieval size, and refuses it before any token is spent if the estimate exceeds a remaining budget.

requirements.source: architecture §24 Quotas, budgets and cost control
requirements.requirement: Actual usage is recorded against person, department, agent, model and lane and linked to the request it paid for, and the estimator is corrected from actuals.

requirements.source: architecture §24 Quotas, budgets and cost control; needs-rupash 38
requirements.requirement: When a budget is hit the person is told which budget and who can raise it, and at a department ceiling the department admin is warned and further questions are refused until the next period.

requirements.source: architecture §24 Quotas, budgets and cost control
requirements.requirement: The publish gate shows a cost per run measured from rehearsal, and publishing an agent whose median run exceeds the department's per-run ceiling needs the Department Admin's approval.

requirements.source: architecture §24 Quotas, budgets and cost control
requirements.requirement: Fan-out is a separate grant: an agent may not spawn parallel workers unless explicitly permitted.

requirements.source: architecture §24 Quotas, budgets and cost control
requirements.requirement: The console shows spend by department, user, agent, model and lane for any period, with machine traffic excluded and labelled.

requirements.source: architecture §24 Quotas, budgets and cost control
requirements.requirement: The console shows cost per answer as a distribution rather than only the mean, and the most expensive agents and question shapes.

requirements.source: architecture §24 Quotas, budgets and cost control
requirements.requirement: The console shows budget consumption against pace, so a department sees mid-month that it is on track to exhaust its budget.

requirements.source: architecture §24 Quotas, budgets and cost control
requirements.requirement: The console lists every refusal and degradation with the budget that caused it.

requirements.source: architecture §24 Quotas, budgets and cost control
requirements.requirement: Because the company holds its own provider keys, metered spend can be reconciled against each provider's own invoice.

Every shared resource has a global budget enforced centrally before work starts: concurrent model calls, concurrent calls per connector, browser sessions, long-running tasks, document jobs, embedding jobs and tokens per minute, each a configuration row.

Under pressure the fast lane still runs, answers queue briefly, tasks queue, browser work queues separately, ingestion throttles and reports are deprioritised, and a queued person sees their position and expected wait.
Interactive, background and batch work run in three classes with separate database pools and budgets, so an ingestion run cannot slow chat.

Every side-effecting operation carries an idempotency key and moves through pending, sent, unknown, verifying and succeeded or failed, and an unknown outcome after a crash is resolved by checking the target system, never by a blind retry.
Every connector that writes implements a read-back that answers whether an operation landed, and a connector that cannot is restricted to read-only tools, declared in its manifest.
A worker killed immediately after any side-effect boundary recovers without repeating the action.
Independent source calls for one question run concurrently and the latency budget covers the slowest call rather than the sum, while per-source and global call budgets still apply.

A token bucket, circuit breaker and retry policy sit in front of every external system, owned by the connector layer, tracking requests per second and minute, concurrency, rate-limit responses, latency and errors against configured ceilings.
Browser work has its own scheduler with global concurrency, memory and CPU limits, per-domain and per-agent limits, and a global kill switch.

Service levels are targets measured from the ledger: fast lane p50 under 100ms and p95 under 500ms, answer lane p50 under 4s and p95 under 8s, task acknowledgement under 1s, permission decision p95 under 50ms, redaction p95 under 20ms, successful requests above 99.5 per cent.
Unintended disclosure has a target of zero, checked continuously by permission canaries in production.

Every request records its trace id, principal, agent version, policy epoch, entitlement hash, lane, model, provider, time to first token, input and output tokens, tool count and latency, connector, cache hit, redaction count, fallback count, retry count and final status.

requirements.source: architecture §25 Capacity, failure and SLOs; needs-rupash 46
requirements.requirement: Each deployment profile states a recovery point and recovery time that go into the client agreement and are backed by the means that deliver them.
The single box is the default, and a split into an application-and-browser host and a database-and-object-store host is designed now and built on a trigger with no application change.

A failure-mode matrix gives every component its failure, user impact, recovery path and data risk, and classifies every operation as safe to retry, unsafe, retry only after verification, or needing a person.

A chaos suite kills the database, the model provider, a connector mid-call, the browser and the worker mid-task, injects malformed JSON and rate limits, fills the disk, and changes a policy or disables a user during an active task, and the system recovers correctly each time.
The first stage is accepted when twenty real questions from five real people are answered correctly, the permission decision on each is explainable, and a restore drill has completed.
A department admin installs an agent that answers correctly within minutes, and a worker killed mid-task recovers without repeating the action.
A model can be swapped without fear, because a routing change is checked against the golden questions before it takes traffic and time and money per request are visible.
Two departments are in real use across two channels.
The brain does real work and can read a client portal that has no API.
One real browser write against one target runs behind the Assisted rung.
The Autonomous rung, confidence scoring and memory promotion are built only after the earlier stages have produced real outcome labels.

requirements.source: architecture §26 Build plan (sequencing); owner brief change 9
requirements.requirement: Depth before breadth: one complete maintenance agent (Lark channel, ticket desk connector, uploaded maintenance knowledge, one workflow, one approval) runs on the owner's install, with a worker and a vault, before breadth work.
Retrieval works across languages, including lexical search that segments Chinese correctly and mixed-language documents.
PII recognition covers the local national identity number and company registration formats and local name forms.
Streaming answers are safe for screen readers: announced on completion rather than token by token, with a skip-to-answer control.
The console and member application work on a phone, at minimum for approvals, and can be installed as a web app.
A conversation can be exported by its owner, and a bulk export for eDiscovery requires a reason and writes an audit row.

Retention runs per data class with a report, and a subject access or deletion request covers every store (rows, projections, memory, traces, recordings, backups) with a certificate of what was removed.
Questions touching HR, grievances or whistleblowing are intercepted and handled on a separate path.
The API is versioned with a stated deprecation policy.
A person can ask the Brain or invoke an agent from Lark.
A person can ask the Brain or invoke an agent from WhatsApp.
A person can ask the Brain or invoke an agent from Slack.
A person can ask the Brain or invoke an agent by email.
A person can ask the Brain or invoke an agent from the web application.
A further channel can be added later through the channel adapter contract without changing the gate or any agent.
An agent is reachable only on the channels an administrator enabled for it, and never automatically on every channel.
A per-agent channel list can only narrow what a run may carry; enabling a channel for an agent never adds reach that the channel or the asker lacks.
Google Drive can be connected and read, scoped at connect to the folders it was given.
Lark data (Base and Wiki) can be connected and read.
Slack can be connected as a data source that reads only invited channels and never returns a message the asker cannot see in Slack.
Freshdesk can be connected and its tickets read at the asker's reach.
Xero can be connected and read.
A CRM can be connected and read.
The maintenance portal (the company's own maintenance records application) can be connected and read.
A domain and hosting system can be connected, reporting each client domain's registrar, expiry and hosting status.
Cloudflare can be connected, reading zones, DNS records and security events.
Google Workspace can be connected with its services chosen at connect, and mail and calendar are read with the asking person's own authorisation.
Google Analytics can be connected and read for a bound property and a named date range.
Search Console can be connected and read for a verified site and a named date range.
Any other API or business system can be connected (MCP server, OpenAPI specification with field mapping, or a sandboxed custom adapter) and becomes available to agents after review without a release.
Each connector is a separate module that is connected, configured and switched off independently from the console.
An agent run receives only the connectors it is authorised to use, and a call to any other connector is refused even when the asker could reach that source directly.
An agent can use a connected system's data to act, not only to read it, with every write a deliberate grant that runs only as an approved prepared action and is verified by reading it back.
A connector attached to an agent is a setting compiled into that agent's ceiling, resolved by the same intersection as every other ceiling entry, and not a second permission system.

The knowledge base holds SOPs, policies, pricing notes, FAQs, service information, company rules, best practices, templates and training material, each item tagged with its kind and retrievable by kind.
Department knowledge is held in the same knowledge base and reaches only people whose scope covers that department.
An approved previous solution becomes company knowledge only after a named person approves it, recording what it solved, who approved it and when.
Company templates held as knowledge are used by agents to produce documents, decks and spreadsheets.
Institutional knowledge is a store of its own, separate from connectors, which provide live external data that is never copied into the knowledge base.
An administrator adds knowledge from the console and it is answered from on the install.
An administrator creates a skill from scratch in the console.
A skill can be imported (from a repository at a pinned commit, a URL or an uploaded archive) and cannot run until it is reviewed.
An administrator edits a skill in the console, and the edit is saved as a new version awaiting review while every agent keeps its pinned version until moved.
Skills are versioned, and a new version is reviewed against a diff of the previous one.
An administrator assigns a skill to an agent, only from the approved library.
A skill assigned to an agent actually changes what that agent's runs do.
An administrator removes a skill from an agent, and the detachment is kept in history.
The same approved skill is reused by several agents as one library item rather than copied into each.
An approved skill can be exported as a package another install imports, carrying its version and digest and landing unreviewed there.
A skill declares the knowledge it needs, and assigning it to an agent whose knowledge scope does not cover that need is refused with what is missing.
A skill declares the tools it needs, and they are checked against the agent's ceiling before the assignment is written.
A skill carries its instructions, loaded by the agent by name and description first and in full on demand.
A skill carries example tasks with expected behaviour, and a new version cannot be approved until they have been rehearsed against it.

Skills of the kinds the owner named can be built and run: SEO audit, keyword research, website health check, ticket analysis, client complaint analysis, monthly SEO report, proposal generation and website troubleshooting.
A skill is a reusable capability stored in the library and referenced by agents, never hardcoded into one agent.
A Maintenance agent exists as a specialised agent.
An SEO agent exists as a specialised agent.
A Sales agent exists as a specialised agent.
A Finance agent exists as a specialised agent.
A Support agent exists as a specialised agent.
A Project Management agent exists as a specialised agent.
Each agent is configured with which skills it has.
Each agent is configured with which knowledge it can access, as a scope rather than a document list.
Each agent is configured with which connectors it can use.
Each agent is configured with which channels can invoke it.
Each agent is configured with which tools it can use.
Each agent is configured with which workflows it can execute, and it runs no other workflow.
Each agent is configured with the permissions it has, as a ceiling that only narrows the asker's reach.
Each agent is configured with which actions require human approval.
Each agent is configured with which memory and context it can access.
An agent is a configurable worker composed of separately managed parts, not a prompt or personality.
An administrator creates and configures a workflow from the console as stored, versioned data.
A workflow breaks a larger task into steps that run without the person performing each one.
A workflow step can call a skill.
A workflow step can retrieve information from a connector, and different steps can read different connectors.
A workflow step can use a tool, under the gate, leash and meter as an agent's own call.
Results pass between workflow steps as named, schema-checked outputs.
Workflow steps run in sequence or, where declared, in parallel.
A workflow step can run only when a condition over earlier outputs holds, and a skipped step is recorded with its condition.
A failing workflow step is retried within its own limit and then takes its declared failure path, with side-effecting steps retried only through their idempotency key.
A workflow step can request human approval and the workflow continues after the decision.
A workflow combines intermediate results in a step that waits for every parallel branch or records the gap.
A workflow produces and delivers a final output.

requirements.source: owner brief §6 Workflows example: SEO Monthly Report
requirements.requirement: A monthly SEO report is prepared end to end by a workflow: identify the client, read analytics and search console data, read the previous report, analyse changes, run SEO checks, identify issues, write recommendations, prepare the report, ask for approval where required and deliver it.

requirements.source: owner brief §6 Workflows example: SEO Monthly Report, step 1
requirements.requirement: A workflow identifies the client a request is about from the name a person used, and states the ambiguity rather than guessing when two clients match.

requirements.source: owner brief §6 Workflows example: SEO Monthly Report, step 4
requirements.requirement: A workflow retrieves the previous report produced for the same client and report type, at the asker's reach.
A coordinating agent delegates subtasks of a complex request to other specialised agents.
Delegated subtasks run in parallel where they are independent, within depth and concurrency caps.
The coordinating agent combines the specialists' checked results into one final output, stating any gap from a failed subtask.

requirements.source: owner brief §7 Multi-Agent / Multi-Task Execution example: SEO improvement proposal
requirements.requirement: A request to analyse a client's website and prepare a complete SEO improvement proposal is decomposed into website analysis, SEO data analysis, competitor analysis, a check of company services and pricing, and recommendations, handled by separate agents and consolidated by a coordinator.
The current conversation is kept as context for the turn and dies with the thread.
Task and workflow context (earlier steps' outputs and state) is available to later steps and survives a restart.
Project context (the project, its client, open tickets and recent decisions) is read from the sources at the asker's reach on every turn and never stored as a memory.
User context (what is remembered about the asker) is shown to the model as hints the asker may still recall, never cited as a source.
Agent memory is kept per agent and shown separately from memory about people.
Company knowledge is part of the context a turn is assembled from, at the asker's reach.
Long-term learned information is held with a confidence that decays unless reinforced and is superseded on contradiction.
The kinds of context are kept distinct, and each turn's trace names which were included and which were left out.
Memory is permission-aware: a memory carries the reach it was formed under and is not replayed to anyone who could not see what formed it.
Memory is controlled: a person can read, edit and delete what is remembered, and an administrator sets how long inferred memories last.
The system does not store everything: only listed kinds of observation become memories, and a field value read from a source is never stored as one.
One context assembler reads the existing stores for each turn, rather than seven separate memory stores, and project and user context are re-read each time.

requirements.source: owner brief §9 Tools / Browser / Computer Use
requirements.requirement: An agent can call external APIs as typed tools.

requirements.source: owner brief §9 Tools / Browser / Computer Use
requirements.requirement: An agent can call MCP tools, pinned so a silent redefinition fails closed.

requirements.source: owner brief §9 Tools / Browser / Computer Use
requirements.requirement: An agent can execute code in a sandbox.

requirements.source: owner brief §9 Tools / Browser / Computer Use
requirements.requirement: An agent can control a browser.

requirements.source: owner brief §9 Tools / Browser / Computer Use
requirements.requirement: An agent can use computer-use capabilities (operating a desktop application), deferred behind browser checks.

requirements.source: owner brief §9 Tools / Browser / Computer Use
requirements.requirement: An agent can perform file operations: read a file a person attached and store files it produces.

requirements.source: owner brief §9 Tools / Browser / Computer Use
requirements.requirement: An agent can use external AI services other than a chat model, each registered as a tool with a required capability.

requirements.source: owner brief §9 Tools / Browser / Computer Use
requirements.requirement: An agent can generate documents, slide decks and spreadsheets.

requirements.source: owner brief §9 Tools / Browser / Computer Use
requirements.requirement: Other specialised tools can be registered with a required capability, side-effect class and result contract.

requirements.source: owner brief §9 Tools / Browser / Computer Use
requirements.requirement: The agent decides when a tool is needed during a run, and can call only tools its permissions project into its catalogue.

requirements.source: owner brief §9 Tools / Browser / Computer Use example
requirements.requirement: Asked whether a client's website is working, an agent actually opens the website, inspects it, performs checks and analyses the results.
Computer use is a last resort: website checks use HTTP plus a read-only browser, and a browser skill is refused where an API tool exists unless exempted by a named approver.
Computer use is deferred and browser checks are built first; the console shows no computer-use switch until the capability exists.
The harness selects which agent handles a request, and a person can also address a named agent they may use.
The harness selects the model for each call.
The harness assembles the context for each turn.
The harness loads the agent's assigned skills into the run.
The harness gives the run only the agent's bound connectors, with credentials leased per run.
The harness projects the tool catalogue for the run.
The harness enforces permissions on every call: capability, leash rung and field mask.
The harness executes workflows through the one agent runtime.
The harness decomposes tasks into subtasks.
The harness runs parallel steps and subtasks.
The harness aggregates results.
The harness handles human approvals by suspending and resuming the run.
The harness handles errors and retries, including model fallback on a closed set of failures.
The harness logs every run as a trace a person can follow.
The harness enforces cost and token limits before tokens are spent.
The harness applies security screening to input and tool results without letting the screen grant or block access.
The harness holds credentials so no agent or model ever sees a secret value.
The harness reads environment configuration from one settings place, editable from the console where an operator tunes it.
An agent operates only inside the harness and never has unrestricted access to the whole Brain: every entry path uses the one runtime, runs are bounded, and an agent can be halted.
The system learns from user feedback given in the console and in every channel.
A person can give a thumbs up or thumbs down on an answer, stored against the answer's trace.
The system learns from human corrections.
The system learns from outputs a person approved without changes.
The system learns from successful workflow runs.
The system learns from failed workflow runs, and repeated failures of a step open a learning candidate instead of changing the workflow.
Repeated corrections of the same kind are recognised and raised as one learning candidate.
A new SOP changes answers once it is published, superseding the older version.
A new skill improves agents only after it is reviewed and assigned.
Agent evaluations feed learning by opening review candidates, never by changing the agent directly.
A correction never rewrites company knowledge or rules automatically; it becomes a learning candidate that a person reviews and approves before it becomes permanent knowledge or a new rule.
A thumbs up or down is counted but changes nothing by itself; reviewed corrections are what change behaviour.
A correction may carry the right answer in the person's own words, held as a permission-protected learning candidate until approved.
Sending an email to a client stops for a person's approval before it is sent.
Issuing a quotation stops for a person's approval before it is issued.
Changing DNS stops for a person's approval before the change is made.
Making a financial change stops for a person's approval before it is made.
Deleting information stops for a person's approval before anything is deleted.
Publishing content stops for a person's approval before it is published.
Changing a production system stops for a person's approval before the change is made.
An agent prepares a sensitive action, a person approves the exact prepared action, and the system then executes it once without the requester returning.
Approvals are decided only in the console or on Lark cards, never by WhatsApp or email.
An irreversible action needs a second person: it cannot be approved by the person who asked for it or by the principal it runs as.
An administrator may approve a skill they imported themselves, and the approval is recorded as a self-approval.
Channels are created and configured independently of agents.
Knowledge is created and configured independently of agents.
Agents are created and configured independently from the console.
Skills are created and configured independently of agents.
Workflows are created and configured independently of agents.
Tools are managed independently: an administrator sees each registered tool with its capability and side-effect class and can switch one off.
Permissions are managed independently: grants, packs and roles are created and changed from the console.
Memory is configured independently per agent.
Learning rules are configured independently: memory lifetime, promotion thresholds, active tiers and a freeze per agent.
Separately created parts are combined into an agent from console choices alone, with no code change or release.

requirements.source: owner brief §13 Everything Modular composition: Maintenance Agent
requirements.requirement: The Maintenance agent is composed of maintenance knowledge, the Freshdesk connector, the maintenance portal connector, maintenance skills, the Lark channel, the browser tool and maintenance workflows.

requirements.source: owner brief §13 Everything Modular composition: SEO Agent
requirements.requirement: The SEO agent is composed of SEO knowledge, the Analytics connector, the Search Console connector, SEO skills, the Lark or web channel and SEO workflows.
Agent permissions only narrow and never add: a run's reach is the asker's reach intersected with the agent's ceiling.
Pricing is held as classified table rows, where everyone may read the sell price and only holders of the right capability read cost and margin, not as knowledge documents.
Parallel workflow steps that call skills are delivered before multi-agent delegation, which is built last.
Depth before breadth: one complete Maintenance agent works on the first install (Lark, Freshdesk, uploaded maintenance knowledge, one workflow and one approval) before other agents are broadened.

requirements.source: owner brief approved change 9 and decision D3
requirements.requirement: The first install runs the worker and the vault (key store).
Connector keys live in the vault, are written once and are never read back or shown.
Workflows may contain model and skill steps, and those steps run only through the one agent runtime.
A delegated specialist runs at the asker's reach intersected with the specialist's own ceiling, and delegation happens only along links an administrator set.

requirements.source: requirements-audit §1 Asked for, and in the document
requirements.requirement: The system is client-hosted: nothing runs on the builder's infrastructure, and one install serves one company on its own server.

requirements.source: requirements-audit §1 Asked for, and in the document
requirements.requirement: Redaction is field-level and capability-driven at request time: on one client record one person sees hours remaining and not contract value while another sees both.

requirements.source: requirements-audit §1 Asked for, and in the document
requirements.requirement: One gate decides every request in a stated order: identify, entitle, screen, cache, route, project tools, then redact.

requirements.source: requirements-audit §1 Asked for, and in the document
requirements.requirement: Platform roles cover the employee (member), the department admin and the platform admin (super admin), with the installing partner as a principal kind.

requirements.source: requirements-audit §1 Asked for, and in the document
requirements.requirement: Departments are scopes over one database rather than separate deployments, so adding a department is configuration.

requirements.source: requirements-audit §1 Asked for, and in the document
requirements.requirement: Knowledge, Skills, Tools and the Leash are the four nouns people configure.

requirements.source: requirements-audit §1 Asked for, and in the document
requirements.requirement: Requests run in three lanes, FAST with no model, ANSWER in process and TASK durable, chosen by deterministic rules.

requirements.source: requirements-audit §1 Asked for, and in the document
requirements.requirement: An autonomy ladder (Shadow, Assisted, Autonomous) is set per agent, action target and scope.

requirements.source: requirements-audit §1 Asked for, and in the document
requirements.requirement: A web-agency agent template catalogue ships, with a first set usable on day one.

requirements.source: requirements-audit §1 Asked for, and in the document
requirements.requirement: Agents come from signed, versioned templates, with opt-in upgrades and client-authored templates.

requirements.source: requirements-audit §1 Asked for, and in the document
requirements.requirement: Skill building, assigning to agents and importing from GitHub are one architecture.

requirements.source: requirements-audit §1 Asked for, and in the document
requirements.requirement: Skills use the SKILL.md folder format, and connectors support MCP.

requirements.source: requirements-audit §1 Asked for, and in the document
requirements.requirement: Whether to fan out is decided and justified against measured cost, and every run records the fan-out verdict and its counterfactual.

requirements.source: requirements-audit §1 Asked for, and in the document
requirements.requirement: Memory is a day-one subsystem with three kinds: session, persistent and adaptive.

requirements.source: requirements-audit §1 Asked for, and in the document
requirements.requirement: A visual builder lets agents be composed without code (a form composer plus a bounded procedure canvas and a read-only trace graph).

One secure console lets an authorised administrator manage, configure, monitor and control the whole platform without touching the server, the database, the source or a configuration file for anything routine.

Every control is proved to reach the system: its write is followed to the row, to the audit entry and to the behaviour it changes, and a control that reaches nothing is not shipped as working.

Nothing sensitive is displayed: a credential is written once and never read back, and a screen shows only that a secret is held.
A destructive action is confirmed, and the confirmation says what will happen and to what.
Validation happens before the write, and an error says what to do about it.
Loading, empty, unreachable and failed are different written states on every screen, never one blank panel.
Success and failure are both reported in words a person can act on.
Long lists page, search, filter and sort, with bulk actions where they are safe.
Every console screen works at phone width.
Every console screen works from the keyboard.
Navigation is grouped by what an administrator is trying to do, as one coherent platform rather than a drawer of settings pages.

requirements.source: admin-console §Before any of this is called done
requirements.requirement: Before the console is called done, everything an administrator needs is listed from the schema, modules, routes and settings, compared screen by screen, and each gap built or recorded with its reason.
A dashboard gives the administrator a company overview as the landing screen.
Usage, limits and budgets are managed from the console, budgets as money ceilings per company, department, person or agent.
API configuration is managed from the console: service accounts and API keys created, shown once, rotated and revoked.
An agent is created from a template or from scratch through saved drafts, a rehearsal and a publish that a second person approves.
An agent's information (name, summary, owner and audience) is set and changed from the console.
An agent's instructions and behaviour are set from the console.
An agent's model and provider are chosen from the console.
An agent is tested from the console by rehearsing it as a named person through the real gate before publishing.
An agent is edited through a new draft, duplicated, enabled, disabled, archived and handed over from the console.
An agent's version and template lineage are visible, with upgrades offered and declinable.

Agent templates are browsed, searched and filtered, each showing what it carries, its required and optional skills and connectors with readiness, and its intended permissions as requested rather than granted.
An agent is created from a template and customised, with the template's sealed paths shown locked with the reason.
A template is authored from an agent through a scan for company details, published as a new version, and withdrawn from the catalogue.
A skill import is approved or rejected in a review queue.
A skill is retired (archived) and reinstated in the library, and detached from an agent, without deleting its history.
A skill is tested by rehearsing an agent that holds it.
The console shows which agents currently use a skill.
Connectors available to connect and connectors connected are shown apart, and a connected source nothing reads is never shown healthy.
An administrator tests a connection from the console.
An administrator replaces a connector's key, edits its configuration as one change, reconnects and disconnects it from the console.
Connector status and health are shown, and drift from what was agreed at connect is flagged.

requirements.source: admin-console-architecture §4.4 who can access what, and why

requirements.source: admin-console-architecture §4.4 who can access what, and why
requirements.requirement: For a capability, the console lists every holder, the scope of each grant and its origin.

Every console module offers list, search, filter, sort, paging, detail, create, edit, archive, reinstate, enable or disable, duplicate, import, export, bulk actions, validation, confirmation, feedback, permission and audit history wherever each applies, and says why where one does not.
The setup wizard names a data steward who is granted each connected source's declared capabilities, so data access starts with a named, audited person and never with the administrator by default.
An agent's page has Dashboard, Profile and About views, with spend, skill count and age in its header, and an About view anybody can read that is derived from the agent's real configuration.
A plug-in interface is written only when a real replacement part exists to test it; the nine listed plug-in points are recorded as not needed yet.
requirements.decision: needs-rupash 58: a plugin interface is written when a real plugin for it exists

requirements.requirement: The administrative consoles of the platform's own components stay on public addresses, protected by a second login factor and an IP allowlist, and the install documentation says so.
An install deploys by pulling new releases itself, needing no inbound access and no deploy secrets held by the code host.
A new image is deployed only after its signature is verified, and a change is detected by the registry digest rather than the tag.
Backups are kept as thirty daily copies plus weekly copies to day thirty-five, so no copy outlives the 35-day horizon every erasure certificate promises.
Every spend record links to the trace of the request it paid for, and the trace records tool count and fan-out, so the most expensive question shapes are ranked from one join.
An automation runs as the person who owns it, narrowed by the automation's own limit, loses access the moment its owner does, and stops for adoption when its owner leaves.
Probabilistic record matching runs in its own offline image, produces suggestions a person confirms, and never runs on the path that answers a question.
An install refuses to start unless the image and release it runs are named, and one setting holds the whole install at that release.
A client never receives a copy of the repository: the installer fetches one archive of one release tag, and the published archive is checked to carry no client value.
requirements.decision: needs-rupash 77: the product lives only in rpsj2230/Verz-OS-v2.0; the owner's other repositories are out of scope

requirements.requirement: One licence allowlist serves every image, accepting permissive licences (including 0BSD, Zlib, CC0 and MIT-0) and still refusing copyleft.
Readiness reports sign-in as its own part: a wrong identity provider issuer keeps the site up, refuses sign-in and names sign-in as not ready.
The embedding width is an install setting, a width the vector index cannot support is refused, and changing the width is refused while any chunk holds a vector.

A supervision pin on an agent that touches money is reviewed at thirty days against a measured confidence; below 90 percent the supervised period extends, supervision ends only at 90 percent or above, and the pin never expires on a timer.
The SEM agent may prepare a budget change but cannot apply one; the gate, not its instructions, enforces that a person commits it.
Evaluation asks every golden question through the real gate as each persona, never against a bare model, and a regression blocks the merge.

Routine people, grant and joiner-mover-leaver administration happens in the product console with staff arriving from the directory, so nobody opens the identity provider's own console for routine work.
When a budget is reached, the department admin is warned and further questions charged to it are refused until the next period.
The stop button halts at once with no confirmation and no second signature; resuming needs a written reason and says when one person overrides another; a halt survives a restart and never expires.
A department admin has a stop button for their own department.
A department admin gets every console screen the requirements call for, narrowed to their scope, except the screens about the installation itself (backup, this install, rate limits, capacity).
A filter dropdown offers only departments and people the reader can already reach.
The console offers a company overview, every screen filterable by department and person, all activity, budget and spend, and a global stop button.
The staff source is chosen per install at setup (spreadsheet, Google Sheet, Google Workspace, Microsoft, Lark or a directory), never fixed in the product.
A staff list asserts only that a person exists by default; departments and roles are set in the console, and what a source may assert can change per source without a migration.
Exactly one implementation turns a scope into a query, and a check catches a second copy even under another name.
Every service that connects to the application database has a declared connection bound, and a worker whose pool size is undeclared refuses to start.
A fresh install creates every settings file its containers read, creates the trace ledger's own database and role, and describes the object store once.
A nightly database copy is written to the backups store with a manifest beside it, and 'last verified restore' reads never verified until a drill has restored a copy.
Every read of a personnel record or a salary-bearing record is written as an audit event, so a member can see which agents read their HR record.

The service level statement promises the chosen profile's recovery point and time, and is refused until a restore drill has verified a copy and the newest real copy is inside the promised recovery point.
Scheduled safety mechanisms run from a scheduler inside the application, holding a database lock so two copies never run the same job, while the audit anchor keeps its external timer.
The retention sweep first runs as a dry run reporting what it would remove, and removes nothing until a person releases it.

A department head reads their department's activity through audit grants over the people placed in the department, which the staff sync rewrites on join and leave, and no audit entry records a department.

A migration cutover cannot be recorded complete while any security act (revoking the old system's authorisations, recording when its access ended, the restore drill) is unrecorded, and progress reports buildable work and acts separately.
Parsing, name-recognition and embedding models run behind a separate inference server and never inside the application image.
The optional automation canvas reaches the Brain over an internal network only and has no route to the internet.
The website chat widget needs no login and answers an anonymous visitor only from knowledge explicitly marked public.
Knowledge is marked public only by a super admin, or by a department admin for their own department's items, and each marking is audited naming the person.
Widget sessions are rate-limited and capped per origin and expire sooner than a signed-in session.

An answer names a source that could not be reached only when the asker could already see that source; anyone else is told part of the answer is unavailable, and the full list goes to the operator log.
Deployment history is kept apart from the permission audit trail and never appears in a client's compliance export.
Every push to the main branch deploys, reaching production automatically once staging has passed the same commit, with no manual tagging.
requirements.decision: needs-rupash 82: the owner's server is the first company's production install; later companies get their own server via the installer

requirements.requirement: Roles that come from the directory live in their own table owned by the sync, which can remove rows only there, keyed by person, role and group.
A person's id is minted by the product and the identity provider's subject maps to it, so replacing the provider rewrites no id, grant or audit row.
A session ends after 30 minutes idle and 10 hours absolute, offline sessions are bounded, and the identity provider and the product agree on both limits.
The vault opens with any three of five key shares whose holders are not all on call, and its root token is revoked after setup; the console shows this policy but cannot change it.
The approve permission alone decides who may approve; the Approver role is a label, and holding one without the other is flagged as a misconfiguration.
A break-glass session lasts four hours by default, is set per grant and expires on its own.
An approval card is rendered at the approver's own reach, carries no value from the requester's data, and ignores a press from anyone other than the person it was rendered for.
When more than one leash rule applies to an action, the strictest wins.
A channel adapter renders a payload's unredacted label or refuses to send it.
A field that counts a collection is withheld whenever that collection is filtered for the asker, so a hidden count cannot be worked out by subtraction.
When a request exceeds even the largest model, retrieval is trimmed and the request retried, the answer says it drew on fewer sources, and nothing is truncated silently.
A model's refusal on its own content rules never makes the system try another model; the refusal is given once and recorded.
The head of the audit chain is published daily somewhere the database administrator cannot write, so deleting the newest entries is detected.
Capability names may appear in the audit ledger as a named exception, so the audit view can say what was granted.
The audit ledger records which fields changed, never their values.

Moving off a previous agent platform imports its skills rather than rewriting them, rebuilds its agents from templates starting at Shadow, carries none of its learning, and revokes its authorisations before the subscription ends.

Retiring a department is refused while live grants are bounded by its scope unless they are moved first, and a newly created department's scope can be granted at once.

A department's page shows its members, lead history, its scope in words, the agents whose audience it is and its knowledge coverage, and the structure can be imported from the staff source's organisation plan.

requirements.source: admin-console-architecture §2.3 B3; §3.1 B3; §6 R3; §7 checklist B3
requirements.requirement: Capability packs are created, versioned, copied, retired and assigned from the console with confirmation and an audit entry, appointing a role within a scope grants no capability, and there is no editor for what a role grants.
Nobody certifies their own grant in an access review, an approved elevation lapses within four hours, and access friction shows refusal patterns by shape without naming the capability or record.

Unlinking the last administrator's sign-in is refused, a spreadsheet staff source cannot appoint a role, a person's sessions can all be ended as one act, a sign-in can be re-linked after unlinking, and the session policy is shown.

A service account has an owner and a declared ceiling and resolves its owner's live entitlements narrowed by that ceiling with no grants of its own; a third live key is refused; a key can never approve or administer; the owner can be changed and the account expired.

The agents list shows each agent's audience, owner, state, tier, leash summary, template and version, and its runs and cost over thirty days, searchable and filterable by department, state and template, and an agent's page lists its recent runs.
An agent's manifest can be exported as a document and imported from a file through the company-detail scan.
Publishing an agent, every lifecycle move and every leash move leaves an audit entry, and an agent's History tab filters the audit log by that agent.
An agent's Dashboard shows the approvals waiting on that agent, counted only over cards this reader could decide, and approval cards carry the agent and filter by it.
One Approvals queue holds suspended actions, second approvals for a widened publish and leash promotions, and none of them can be decided by their own author.

An agent can be added to a chat group, answered at the floor of everybody present, without granting the room anything, and each channel on the agent is switched on per agent from what its caller's run could carry.
An agent's availability can name individual people and more than one department, as discovery only.
Each agent has a learning switch that pauses memory formation and learning for that agent.
An agent can be given browser use from its Profile, with the browser tools held in its ceiling through the publish gate.
An agent can operate a desktop application (computer use).

An agent carries a plain-text overview of up to 1,200 characters that a company can edit, that the leak scan covers and that is never passed to a model, with template documents moved to a new schema version so signed templates still verify.

requirements.requirement: A figure nothing stores reads 'not recorded yet' rather than zero, and every money figure carries the install's currency.
An agent's leash is shown per target with its rung history and circuit-breaker demotions, lowered at once and raised only with evidence and a named approver.

Built-in templates are signed with an install key held in the vault, and an install with no vault says installing a template is unavailable rather than keeping the key somewhere weaker.
The Skills module has a Tools tab listing every tool in the registry with its capability and side effect.
An approved skill can be exported from the console.
An ownerless automation can be adopted, an automation can be installed again for another owner, a resumed automation starts on the next tick, and removal stops it while keeping its history.

Routing rungs are added, retired and reordered as insert-only positions, switching a provider off removes its rungs from the next plan, a provider check is one metered call, and the routing configuration exports.
A connector's connection record can be exported without its keys.

A knowledge owner verifies, sets a review date on, supersedes, archives, bulk re-verifies and exports documents from the console, promoting wider visibility needs a separate approval, and an administrator sees that an item exists and how widely it reaches, never its contents.
Tier-two learning is promoted and tier-three learning decided from the console with the agreement recorded, a person edits their own memory, and learning and memory export.
A proposed field classification is applied only by a second person, fast-path rules are listed, and entity merges are reviewed from the console.
Re-downloading an artifact re-checks the requester's reach at that moment, and artifact reads are auditable.
The Channels screen shows for each surface whether it is configured, its inbound verification check, the verbs it may carry and its rooms with their floor, and each surface can be switched off.
A switched-off webhook can be switched back on, an exhausted delivery can be replayed, and deliveries after a secret change verify with the new secret only.
The notifications screen says for each notice whether anything sends it, a switched-off notice sends nothing, and the test message sends once per configuration.

An administrator acknowledges an alert from the System health screen, which covers readiness, the worker, the vault, object storage, the identity provider, breakers, halts and budget stops at company scope only.
Live runs and the queue are listed, and resolving a side effect in an unknown state is confirmed because it cannot be undone.
Background jobs show a history of runs beyond the last, state which controls have no runner, and a pause holds across a restart while run now still starts a paused job.
Logs, audit entries and every report, including the unanswered questions, export from the console carrying only what the exporter may read.
The audit log can be filtered by agent or other subject, not only searched as text.
Changing identity provider values re-derives the redirect addresses, the embedding size refuses a change once anything is embedded, and settings writes need their own admin capability.
Traces are exported to the destination configured in Settings.

The credentials screen lists every vault slot (provider keys, relay password, connector keys, webhook secrets, object store key) with whether it is held, when and by whom written, whether an environment variable outranks it, and the vault's state.
