requirements.requirement: For every model provider the install uses, the company can show a record of which region processes and stores its data, the provider's retention and training terms, the data processing agreement, and exactly what categories of data are sent.
An assignment of a skill to an agent changes that agent's runs, and until a run reads it every assignment on screen says plainly that it is not yet read by a run.

Every step of a skill's life (import, review, assignment, replacement, detachment, retirement, reinstatement) is a new row; nothing is updated or deleted, and current assignments are those with no later detachment or replacement.
A retired skill cannot be newly assigned, and its live assignments are listed for detachment rather than removed silently.
Enabling and disabling a skill is retire and reinstate in the library and detach at the agent; there is no third switch answering whether an agent uses a skill.
An administrator may approve a skill they imported themselves, and the approval is recorded as a self-approval (owner decision D4)
A skill can be imported from a repository or link once network egress for that fetch is ruled, and until then the import screen says why only upload and paste are offered.
A skill with scripts can be imported because its digest covers every script's bytes, so a changed script is a different skill that needs its own review.
The list of agents using a skill holds current assignments only, narrowed to agents the reader may see, paged by cursor, with no count beyond the page.

Before an assignment is written each tool the skill declares is checked against the agent's ceiling, a tool outside it is shown as requested and not in the ceiling, and the check never widens the ceiling (widening is a manifest edit through the publish gate).

Each available source states what it reads, its access mode in words, the key it asks for and its verified ceiling or 'not measured', and a source that cannot be connected from the console carries its reason.

A connector's details show its trust sentences, that a credential is held and when and by whom it was written (never the value), its ceiling, the agents whose manifest names it and the skills whose tools come from it.
Testing a connection sends one probe through the connector's own client under its throttle, records the probe, and never returns business rows.
Disconnecting keeps the connection history and the confirmation says the key stays held in the vault; reconnecting writes a new connection row.
Listing connectors needs read access to connectors, and changing one needs administer access over that source.
A person's Access tab groups every grant by origin (granted by a person, from a pack, from an elevation with its lapse, from the directory), is additive only, and never draws a deny.
The Access tab lists platform roles held with the scope bounding each and says that a role grants nothing by itself.

For a person viewing themselves the console lists which of their actions need a second factor in this sign-in; for an administrator viewing somebody else it lists the console's actions and the assurance each needs, never a list derived from that person's grants.
On a person's Access tab an administrator picks an agent and sees its ceiling beside a preview of that person's run computed by the real gate.
'Who can reach this and why' is asked of a capability and a scope and never of a single record, so the console never confirms that a record exists.
The access views never show a count of withheld rows or screens, a department in a filter the reader cannot reach, the reason a record was refused, or a deny.
The sidebar has nine collapsible groups served by the API's navigation answer, marks the active item, and carries no count badges.

At phone width the menu is never hidden: a visible Menu button is the first control after the skip link, opens every group, reaches every entry and returns focus, and the phone-width tests are changed to hold that rather than deleted.

The header carries global search, the Stop button for those who may halt, the theme switch, and the signed-in person with their sign-in strength and a prompt to sign in again with an authenticator when it is not strong.

Global search covers menu entries and people, agents, skills, connectors and templates through each module's own read, returns no totals, gives one answer for no match and not permitted, and keeps no recent-search history in the browser.
Every page shows breadcrumbs of group, module, entity and tab derived from the route table.
A detail page's tabs are child routes, so each tab has its own address.
A short create or edit opens in a drawer that keeps the list in view and returns focus to the control that opened it.
A destructive act is confirmed in place with focus starting on the safe choice, Escape cancelling and focus returning to the opener, including a removal started from a drawer.
Agent creation, template install and first run are wizards with a persistent draft, one step per builder section.
An empty list says what would put a row there and who may do it.
The result of a write appears in a polite toast region beside the inline result; a toast is never the only place a failure is reported and never carries a value withheld elsewhere.
'Cannot do this yet' and 'why you cannot do this here' are rendered by one explanation component from sentences the server serves.

requirements.source: admin-console-architecture §5.3 why it looks out of date
requirements.requirement: Buttons have primary, quiet and danger variants, and the Dashboard draws KPI tiles, a Needs-you list, an activity feed and cards with headed sections as the design of record does.

requirements.source: admin-console-architecture §5.3 why it looks out of date
requirements.requirement: No class is used in markup without a style rule, and every page reports failure through the one shared failure component rather than a private copy.

The redesign keeps each rule-holding test green or changes it in the same commit with its replacement property written down: no token parsing, role checks or fetch outside the client in the browser, browser storage only for the theme, no password input, no positive tab index, no click handler on a non-control, destructive writes only through the confirm component, every new form in the validated-before-write table, every new route with its four state sentences.
Every module page that mounts the data table is a lazy route, the form libraries are held out of the initial bundle, and the command palette and toaster load lazily.
The product's tokens are the design of record's: warm neutrals, state colours held apart from the brand with washes, the lock's own colour, and dark values for every token.

The accent is install configuration, used as a fill with text chosen by measured contrast, darkened when used as text until it passes 4.5:1, never used to encode state, derived by one tested function served with the runtime configuration and tested over a pale, a mid and a dark accent in both themes.
The interface fonts are bundled in the image under their open licence and never fetched from a third party at page load.
A class can only name a token: Tailwind's default palette is removed, no colour literal exists outside the tokens, and a check refuses a colour class naming no token.

shadcn/ui components are copied into the console rather than installed, the generator is not a build dependency, old stylesheets sit in a legacy cascade layer so an old page keeps its look, and a page leaves that layer when its module moves in wave 2 (no big-bang reskin).

Copied components obey the console's rules: no cookie write (refused by the boundary check), the data table registers no client row model and prints no total, a partly-selected checkbox shows indeterminate, and a dialog opened from state returns focus.
The lock stays one element reading 'Restricted' with no icon, restyled only from the tokens.

Every interface part is under MIT, ISC, Apache-2.0 or OFL-1.1; nothing is bought, and a template whose licence does not plainly allow a product many companies install is not used without the vendor's written answer.

The layout tests that read stylesheets are re-pointed at the compiled CSS or moved to the browser harness in the commit that restyles the first page, so phone-width and colour guarantees are never lost silently.
The content security policy either keeps inline styles allowed for the toaster and scroll lock or moves to nonces, as a recorded choice.
The console sends no telemetry and makes no request beyond its own server while a page is used.
At phone width touch targets are at least 44px and nothing is wider than 320px.

A secret field is write-only: never prefilled, never echoed, not offered to autocomplete or spellcheck, and cleared from state as soon as the request leaves, written once and reused by every screen that takes a secret.

The reference screenshots are compared and adapted, never copied (template card facts, creation stepper order, in-place capability add and remove, connector cards, cost on an agent), and the design's rejections are kept: no single on/off adaptive learning toggle, and no browser operator riding the user's own session.
A person can browse a catalogue of the skills they may use, each shown as a card with an icon, name and short description.
Each skill in the catalogue shows how many times it has been used, as the trust signal for whether anyone relies on it.
Every skill description is written as a routing instruction that begins by saying when to use the skill.
A person can search the skill catalogue and narrow it by category chips.
A person can try a skill straight from its card, starting a conversation that uses that skill.
A person can share a skill they wrote beyond themselves.
The member application has a task starting point separate from talking to a named agent, so a person can start a job without choosing an agent first.
A person sees their recent tasks and threads with each one's state: running, waiting for approval, done or failed.
A person can search their own history.
A person has a library of files and outputs produced for them.
A person can group their own threads and files into a named project whose contents are read as project context.
A person can create a skill by describing it in conversation, and the system drafts it.
A person can write a skill's instructions directly.
A person can import a skill from a GitHub repository.
A person can upload a skill package from their device.
The agent side of the member application has a short navigation: new chat, agents, connectors and skills.
Agents a person can use are listed in two groups, shared team or department agents and their own personal agents.
The composer accepts a message or a task, an attached file and dictated speech.
A catalogue of predefined agents lets an administrator deploy a ready specialist quickly.
Each catalogue card shows the agent's picture, name, one-line role and a single hire action.
A browser agent carries out web tasks.
A computer-operator agent works desktop applications by clicking and typing.
Ready agents include a support agent answering from the knowledge base and a sales assistant.
A person has notifications reachable from the navigation.
A person can create a custom agent by describing it in conversation.
A person can set up a custom agent manually, choosing each part.
Opening an agent shows a workspace with sections for conversations, automations, people, knowledge and memory.
The agent's conversations list can be narrowed to threads related to me, and each thread shows its participants, last activity, a preview and whether it failed.
The agent dashboard shows headline counts of the agent's administrators and automations.
The agent dashboard charts daily usage over 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, this month or all time, with totals for spend and messages.
An agent has a settings control beside its name.
An agent owns its automations, and a person can create a new one from the agent.
With no automations the tab shows an empty state and a gallery of templates to start from.
Automation templates are named as outcomes in the first person.
The template gallery includes a personal daily brief, capturing deals from group chats into the CRM, and drafting replies in the person's voice.
The people list shows each person's role and, under each person, the agents they own.
From an agent a person can add members and agents and change a member's role inline.
A member can lend their own device for an agent to operate.
A person can add knowledge for an agent by extracting it from links.
A person can add knowledge for an agent by uploading files from their device.
An agent shows the artifacts it produced, with a count and an empty state when there are none.
An agent's memory is shown as readable text with its size.
Memory is split between curated memory and memory extracted from chats.
Each memory has a content view and a change history.
An agent keeps a memory of each person it works with, and that person can read it.
Opening an agent's chat shows its picture, name and role description before the first message.
A new chat with an agent offers a few suggested prompts specific to that agent.
An agent's profile header shows spend linked to usage detail, the skill count and how long the agent has existed.
An administrator can add an agent to chat groups from its profile.
An agent's profile has a switch for learning from chats.
The profile lists the agent's connectors as icons with an overflow count and an add control.
The profile lists the agent's skills as chips with an expandable overflow, add and remove.
The profile lists the channels the agent answers on with an add control.
The profile shows which named people and which departments can find and use the agent, each removable.
The profile shows the agent's role description.
The agent page shows its autonomy level, ceiling and model tier, which the reference page lacks.
Connectors are not synced into the Brain: only a minimal index is kept and every business value is read live from the source.

Model providers are online services, OpenAI, Anthropic, Moonshot, DeepSeek and others, switched on from the console; a local-only profile is not required.
Super admins and department admins create agents from their requirements and workflow and assign the skills, tools and other parts each needs.
A template agent installs with one click with sensible defaults, and the wizard stays available.
Delegation is never collapsed into the coordinator by the cost check.
